Os_Lead.Text: While Snapwell is active, stop Windows placement features or replace them with Snapwell actions. Each section compares the two. Previous values are saved and restored when Snapwell is turned off, exits, or next starts after a crash.
Os_DragDescription.Text: Replaces Windows snapping to halves or quarters at the screen edge with Snapwell snapping to cells.
Os_LayoutDescription.Text: Stops together with Snap by dragging.
Os_BarTitle.Text: Snap bar at the top of the screen
Os_BarDescription.Text: Windows 11 22H2 or later. Stops together with Snap by dragging.
Os_ArrowDescription.Text: Replaces these keys with Snapwell actions for left, right, top, and bottom halves.
Os.Error.FutureSnap: This device state is from a newer version. Update Snapwell to change Windows Snap.
Os.Error.Load: Couldn't read device state. Check the file location and permissions, then reopen settings.
Os.Error.FutureArrow: This device state is from a newer version. Update Snapwell to change Win + arrow keys.
Os.Error.SaveArrow: Couldn't save the Win + arrow keys choice. Check the file location and permissions.
Os.Error.FutureRestore: This device state is from a newer version. Update Snapwell to restore Windows behavior.
Os.Error.SaveRestore: Couldn't save the restore choice. Check the file location and permissions.
Os.Consent.Title: Stop Windows Snap?
Os.Consent.Message: Turns off Snap windows in Windows Settings while Snapwell is active. This stops snapping by dragging, the Maximize menu, and the Snap bar together. Previous settings are restored when Snapwell is turned off, exits, or next starts after a crash.
Os.Error.SaveSnap: Couldn't save the Windows Snap choice. Check the file location and permissions.
Os.Diagram.DragName: Snap by dragging: compare with Windows
Os.Diagram.ArrowName: Win + arrow keys: compare with Windows
Os.Diagram.DragBefore: Dragging to an edge or corner shows a gray outline. Release to fill a half or quarter, then choose another window for the remaining space. The same switch also stops these suggestions.
Os.Diagram.DragAfter: No Windows outline appears. Throw and release to highlight the target cells in blue and snap there using springs and magnets. Blue is shown when Zone preview is on. Sizes are not limited to fixed layouts.
Os.Diagram.DragReason: Windows Snap and Snapwell would compete to set the window position and size after release. Snapwell turns off the same Snap windows switch as Windows Settings.
Os.Diagram.LayoutBefore: Hover over Maximize (□) to open a layout menu below it. Choose halves, a 2:1 split, quarters, or another layout to place the window. The first option may show another app's icon to suggest placing them together.
Os.Diagram.LayoutAfter: Hovering over Maximize shows no menu. Clicking it still maximizes the window. Place windows with the launcher (Ctrl+Alt+Space), hotkeys, or dragging.
Os.Diagram.LayoutReason: Windows layouts differ from Snapwell grids and would offer two sets of targets. This menu stops together with Snap by dragging, so it has no separate switch. Registry changes to stop it separately need an Explorer restart.
Os.Diagram.BarBefore: Dragging a window near the top edge shows a row of layouts at the top center. Release over an option to place the window. The first option suggests placing it with another app.
Os.Diagram.BarAfter: No bar appears at the top edge. Moving near it does nothing; Snapwell handles snapping after release with its target preview.
Os.Diagram.BarReason: Prevents Windows and Snapwell from competing. Like the Maximize menu, the bar stops together with Snap by dragging and has no separate switch. This feature requires Windows 11 22H2 or later.
Os.Diagram.ArrowBefore: Moves the window to the left or right half, maximizes it, restores its size, or minimizes it.
Os.Diagram.ArrowAfter: The same keys run Snapwell's left, right, top, and bottom half actions (Ctrl+Alt+arrow keys by default). Half sizes follow Grid and gaps settings.
Os.Diagram.ArrowReason: Windows reserves these keys. A low-level keyboard hook routes them to Snapwell instead of Windows. Turn this off to restore Windows Win + arrow key behavior.
